title: Six-week plan to learn ladder logic well enough for a controls tech interview
summary: A six-week path from contacts and coils to a small PLC project you can explain under interview pressure.

blocks.title: Six weeks to talk ladder like a controls tech
blocks.body: You do not need to master every vendor quirk. You need clean mental models for contacts, coils, timers, counters, and one small program you can walk through out loud. This plan is built for that interview.

items.label: Start/stop station with interlocks you can draw
Explain scan cycle + debug a stuck output

items.title: Contacts, coils, and the scan
items.detail: NO/NC contacts, energize vs latch, and how a PLC reads inputs → solves logic → writes outputs each scan. Draw a simple start/stop latch by hand.

items.title: Timers and sealing circuits
items.detail: TON/TOF/RTO patterns. Add a seal-in start/stop with a fault reset. Practice saying why the seal contact exists.

items.title: Counters, compares, and one-shots
items.detail: CTU/CTD, EQU/GRT style compares, and rising-edge one-shots so you do not double-count. Build a part-count stop.

items.title: Interlocks and safe states
items.detail: E-stop as a hard condition in the logic story (and know what belongs in hardware). Permissives, jam detects, and what 'fail safe' means on a rung.

items.title: I/O, addressing, and a real (or sim) PLC
items.detail: Map digital I/O, force vs toggle carefully, and commission a small program on a trainer or simulator. Document tag names like an adult.

items.title: Interview drills
items.detail: Whiteboard a motor starter ladder from a word problem. Trace a bug: 'output stuck on.' Narrate scan order. Prep two stories from your practice project.

blocks.heading: Each week, do these three things

items.label: Study one pattern until you can redraw it cold
items.detail: Latch, timer, counter, interlock — one per early week.

items.label: Build or modify a tiny program
items.detail: Simulator is fine. Typing rungs beats only watching videos.

items.label: Explain it out loud in under two minutes
items.detail: Interview muscle. Record yourself once a week if that helps.

blocks.heading: Capstone project (finish by week 5)
items: Motor start/stop with seal-in and overload/fault input that drops the seal.
A TON that delays a 'ready' light after start.
A counter that stops the motor after N cycles and requires a reset.
A short written rung-by-rung explanation you could hand an interviewer.

blocks.heading: Likely interview asks → what to practice
rows: NO start, NC stop, seal contact, coil
Time base vs event count; when each fits
Swap one for the other in your project
Trace force, seal path, welded contact story
Inject a bug on purpose in sim
Hardware remove power vs logic permissives
Know what not to put only in software

items.label: Vendor simulator or cheap trainer
items.detail: Pick one ecosystem and stay there for six weeks.

items.label: Ladder logic fundamentals guide
items.detail: Contacts, coils, timers, counters without marketing fluff.

items.label: Your own notebook
items.detail: Hand-drawn rungs stick better than bookmarked tabs.

blocks.title: You are aiming for clear, not encyclopedic
blocks.body: Controls interviews reward people who can narrate a rung and find a fault. Six honest weeks of small programs beat a year of passive video. Show up with one project you understand cold.

blocks.heading: Start this week
blocks.body: Tonight: draw a start/stop latch from memory. This weekend: enter it in a simulator. Week 6 you will be glad you started ugly and early.
